facts.text: False confidence from simulation means trusting a result more than its evidence justifies; the booklet identifies three forms: using a model outside its data, choosing a metric that hides error, and relying on a test protocol that never sampled the dangerous condition.
facts.quote: False confidence is trusting a result more than its evidence justifies

facts.text: The space shuttle Columbia was lost on re-entry on 1 February 2003; after a foam strike at launch, engineers used the Crater impact model to assess tile damage.
facts.quote: The canonical case is the space shuttle Columbia, lost on re-entry on 1 February 2003. After a foam strike at launch, engineers used the Crater impact model to assess tile damage.

facts.text: The Columbia investigation board found that the debris was about 400 times the size in the Crater model's test database; an early briefing reported 640 times.
facts.quote: the debris was about 400 times (an early briefing said 640 times) the size in the model's test database

facts.text: The Columbia investigation board found that when Crater predicted penetration deeper than the tile, engineers used their judgment to conclude that penetration would not be that deep.
facts.quote: when the model predicted penetration deeper than the tile, engineers "used their judgment" to conclude it would not

facts.text: Crater had overpredicted damage for small impacts, and that conservative bias was assumed to hold for the far larger Columbia foam strike.
facts.quote: Crater had overpredicted damage for small impacts, and that conservative bias was assumed to hold for a far larger strike.

facts.text: The Columbia investigation board criticized briefing slides for burying key information in vague words.
facts.quote: The board also criticized briefing slides that buried key information in vague words.

facts.text: A former Columbia program manager argues that Crater warned correctly and management overrode the warning, an alternative view to the investigation board's criticism of model use; the booklet records both views.
facts.quote: A former program manager argues instead that the model warned correctly and management overrode it; the booklet records both views.

facts.text: The booklet identifies two failure modes in the Columbia case regardless of the competing interpretations: using a model outside its validity envelope and human reinterpretation of the model's result.
facts.quote: Either way, two failure modes appear: a model used outside its envelope, and human reinterpretation of its result

facts.text: An aviation seat-certification comparison showed 0.3% peak error but 60.4% time-history error; validating only the peak would have classified the model as excellent.
facts.quote: In aviation seat certification, one comparison showed 0.3% peak error but 60.4% time-history error; validating only the peak would have called the model excellent.

facts.text: A head-injury model passed its validation comparisons but showed a non-conservative tendency, prompting the regulator to limit its use to lower-severity cases.
facts.quote: A head-injury model passed its validation comparisons but showed a non-conservative tendency, so the regulator limited its use to lower-severity cases

facts.text: Independent tests of pedestrian automatic braking on cars found that none of four vehicles avoided a pedestrian at night at 25 mph in 2019.
facts.quote: Independent tests of pedestrian automatic braking on cars found that none of four vehicles avoided a pedestrian at night at 25 mph in 2019

facts.text: By 2025, night avoidance in independent tests of pedestrian automatic braking on cars had improved to 60%.
facts.quote: by 2025 night avoidance had improved to 60%.

facts.text: Daytime pedestrian automatic-braking test protocols for cars had not revealed the sharp decline in pedestrian avoidance at night.
facts.quote: Daytime protocols had not revealed the cliff

facts.text: For the heavy off-road collision-mitigation program, conservative model behavior in light dust does not transfer to dense dust.
facts.quote: conservatism in light dust does not transfer to dense dust

facts.text: For the heavy off-road collision-mitigation program, a single agreement number can hide timing disagreement that changes a collision outcome.
facts.quote: one agreement number can hide timing disagreement that changes a collision outcome

facts.text: A collision-mitigation scenario catalog that omits night, glare or dense dust produces clean results that provide no meaningful evidence for those conditions.
facts.quote: a scenario catalog that omits night, glare or dense dust produces clean results that mean nothing there

facts.text: If the collision-mitigation program's virtual and bench models are wrong, running millions of virtual scenarios produces false confidence.
facts.quote: If the virtual and bench models are wrong, millions of virtual scenarios produce false confidence
